body:
Something like: 
Verify that no direct object references are accessible to users. Instead use only indirect references (e.g. cryptographically strong random values that “map to” the original values).

comments.body:
I'm not convinced that indirect object references are a good solution to the problem. It feels to me that IDORs are simply masking a lack of proper authorisation. Making the underlying objects (through IDORs) doesn't fix the underlying vulnerability, as there's still the possibility of link sharing or accidental Google indexing of 'hidden' objects.

From an architectural perspective, any kind of indirection (like the cryptographically strong random values approach, and many others) can be very hard to scale for heavy traffic sites with global distribution. However, the underlying authorisation problem is something that can be solved a lot easier in most cases.

Thoughts?

> I'm not convinced that indirect object references are a good solution to the problem. It feels to me that IDORs are simply masking a lack of proper authorisation.

100%

title: V4 Access Control: Maybe we should add something about the secure use of direct object references
